episode.title: Cariboo Signals - Cariboo Local Affairs
episode.description:
Riley and Casey explore technology and society in rural communities. Today's focus: Cariboo Local Affairs.

THIS WEEK WE'RE ASKING: Who decides what's worth saving?

NEWS ROUNDUP: We break down [Williams Lake Tribune] Williams Lake Legion cuts ribbon to veterans crosswalk and [Williams Lake Tribune] Okanagan councillor guilty: ‘Used coach position to find boys for companionship’, plus 1 more stories, and explore what these developments mean for communities like ours.

RURAL CONNECTIONS: In the 2026 Cariboo local elections, which candidate records and accomplishments should voters actually evaluate when choosing between incumbents and challengers across four separate ballots? Topics include: The Williams Lake mayoral rematch between Rathor (incumbent, four-year fiscal record) and Cobb (former mayor returning for a fourth term), Rathor's conflict-of-interest complaint as councillor and unresolved 2012-2013 obstruction of justice charge versus his recent public shouting match with Councillor Scott Nelson, The Quesnel mayoral and council races where incumbent Ron Paull and most sitting councillors face minimal opposition, reducing forced candidate distinctions, 100 Mile House's mayoral race as potentially Maureen Pinkney's first contested election after being acclaimed in 2022, CRD electoral area director races (Areas D, E, F) and school trustee races receiving almost no local coverage despite controlling real budget and land-use authority.

Hosts: Riley (Tech optimist with an engineering background) and Casey (Community-first skeptic of tech promises).

COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHT: 100 Mile House Food Bank Society

discussion.central_question: In the 2026 Cariboo local elections, which candidate records and accomplishments should voters actually evaluate when choosing between incumbents and challengers across four separate ballots?
discussion.riley_position: Voters need complete information about all candidates' records—both achievements and complications—to make informed choices, and local media should report systematically on all four ballots (mayoral, council, school trustee, and CRD director races) rather than leaving major races unnamed and uncovered.
riley_key_evidence: Williams Lake has a rematch between incumbent Surinderpal Rathor (who cut city debt by four million dollars) and challenger Walt Cobb (who served as mayor 1990-1996 and 2014-2022)
The CRD Area D, E, and F electoral director races have zero named candidates in available coverage despite deciding land-use and budget authority
School District 27 had a mid-term trustee by-election in 2025 that was rescheduled, but coverage doesn't identify which of the fourteen current candidates is the sitting by-election incumbent
discussion.casey_position: While contested races like Williams Lake's force candidates to draw distinctions and deserve thorough examination, uncontested or barely-covered races (like Quesnel's mostly-incumbent slate and the unnamed CRD seats) get decided by whoever happens to show up and know a name, making systematic reporting and voter attention to all four ballots essential.
casey_key_evidence: Quesnel has eighteen council candidates and an incumbent mayor running largely unopposed, meaning voters must work to find real disagreements that contested races force candidates to articulate

Maureen Pinkney in 100 Mile House was acclaimed to the mayoral seat in 2022 and has never faced a contested election, making her first real electoral test materially different from Cobb and Rathor's established electoral records
Ballot drop-off data (how many voters complete all four ballots versus stopping after mayor) is not publicly reported locally, leaving the actual competitiveness of lower-profile races unmeasurable
discussion.resolution: Riley and Casey agreed to disagree about coverage gaps rather than one conceding; they jointly called on local media to publish complete CRD candidate lists and on listeners to report missing candidate names via email, and requested that Elections BC or local returning officers release post-election ballot completion data to measure whether lower-profile races are genuinely contested or quietly decided by turnout.
